Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

gold.abstract: Due to their widespread applications, linear complementary pairs (LCPs) have attracted much attention in recent years. In this paper, we determine explicit construction of non-special divisors of degree $g$ and $g-1$ on Kummer extensions with specific properties. In addition, we present several methods for constructing LCPs of algebraic geometry codes (AG Codes) via Kummer extensions. These results are applied in constructing explicit LCPs of AG Codes from subcovers of the BM curve, elliptic function fields, hyperelliptic function fields and other function fields. It is important to mention that we construct several families LCPs of MDS AG Codes from elliptic function fields and we obtain some linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from certain maximal elliptic function fields and hyperelliptic function fields.

gold.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of Algebraic Geometry Codes via Kummer Extensions

--- Researcher A ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b: Constructs linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes over finite fields, including explicit elliptic-curve constructions, conditions for dual equivalence, and security parameters (minimum distances) relevant to side-channel/fault-injection countermeasures via direct sum masking.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
LCP-AG codes provide algebraic structure where one code’s dual is equivalent to the other under specific curve-based conditions. This structural duality can be leveraged as an error-detection layer in secure multi-party computation (MPC) protocols: the complementary code pair acts as a verifiable secret-sharing scheme where one share’s integrity check is encoded in the dual code, and the AG-curve geometry supplies arithmetic constraints for malicious-adversary detection.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Hypothesis: Elliptic-curve LCP-AG codes can implement robust verifiable secret sharing with lower communication overhead than generic LCP codes.
Method:
1. Instantiate LCP-AG codes from elliptic curves over F_q (Paper-b construction).
2. Map secret-sharing shares to codewords in C; use D^⊥ for integrity verification.
3. Simulate MPC with malicious adversary injecting faults; measure detection probability using d(C) and d(D^⊥).
4. Compare communication cost and fault-detection rate against random LCP codes and Shamir secret sharing.
Validation: Detection probability ≥ 1 - (q - d(D^⊥))/q; overhead reduction quantified by code length vs. field size.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose using linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes as a substrate for verifiable secret sharing in secure multiparty computation. By exploiting elliptic-curve geometry and dual-code equivalence, our scheme provides fault detection with tunable security parameters while reducing communication overhead compared to generic LCP or Shamir-based approaches. Simulations under malicious fault injection will validate detection rates and efficiency gains.

FINAL IDEA: Use elliptic-curve LCP-AG codes to build a verifiable secret-sharing scheme for MPC where dual-code equivalence provides efficient fault detection with lower communication overhead.

prompts.C|2:
Research task:
Develop a feasible and novel interdisciplinary research idea that genuinely integrates the two source papers. Specify the cross-disciplinary mechanism, a testable research design, and the contribution beyond either paper alone.

Source papers available to you:

These are your colleagues' latest proposals:

--- Researcher B ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-c: Provides algebraic characterizations of linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes, showing that for constacyclic and quasi-cyclic LCP codes, the security parameter min(d(C), d(D⊥)) reduces to a single distance. Also gives binary LCP examples with better parameters than known LCD codes and a linear programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
- The LCP structure (C,D) with D⊥ equivalent to C under constacyclic shifts creates a natural pairing between two code spaces. This pairing can be exploited as a cross-domain mapping: treat C as an error-correcting code for data storage, and D⊥ as a syndrome-decoding space for a physical-layer authentication tag. The equivalence relation becomes an operational bridge: one algebraic object serves two functions (reliability and security) without additional redundancy.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Construct a binary quasi-cyclic LCP pair (C,D) with length n=2m and index 2, using the double circulant examples from paper-c.
- Encode message m ∈ C. Compute syndrome s = H_{D⊥} · y for received word y, where H_{D⊥} is a parity-check matrix of D⊥.
- Test: For a tampering adversary who flips ≤ t bits, measure probability that s remains in the coset of D⊥ corresponding to the original codeword. Compare against a baseline using an LCD code of same length and dimension.
- Validation: Use the linear programming bound from paper-c to show that the LCP scheme achieves the same minimum distance as the best LCD code, while the syndrome check adds a second, independent failure mode that the adversary must satisfy.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose a joint reliability–security coding scheme where a single quasi-cyclic LCP pair (C,D) simultaneously corrects errors via C and authenticates data via the syndrome space of D⊥. The constacyclic equivalence between C and D⊥ reduces the security analysis to one distance parameter, while the double circulant structure enables efficient encoding. Preliminary binary examples from the source paper suggest that this integrated scheme can match or exceed LCD code performance while adding a lightweight integrity check without extra redundancy.

FINAL IDEA: Use the algebraic equivalence between C and D⊥ in quasi-cyclic LCP codes to build a single-code dual-purpose system that corrects errors and authenticates data with no additional redundancy.

- Revised mechanism: Use the single-distance property of quasi-cyclic LCP codes as a lightweight integrity check for a single encoded message, not as a two-share scheme. The syndrome of D⊥ acts as a zero-redundancy authentication tag for data encoded in C.

- Encode message m ∈ C. Compute syndrome s = H_{D⊥} · y for received word y.

- Validation: Use the linear programming bound from Paper-c to show the LCP scheme matches the best LCD minimum distance while adding an independent failure mode for the adversary. Reject Researcher A’s MPC simulation as not grounded in Paper-c.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose a single-code dual-purpose reliability–security scheme using binary quasi-cyclic LCP codes. The constacyclic equivalence between C and D⊥ reduces security analysis to one distance parameter, while the double circulant structure enables efficient encoding. Unlike two-share secret sharing, this scheme adds a zero-redundancy integrity check to error correction, with preliminary examples suggesting performance matching or exceeding LCD codes.

- Paper-c: Provides algebraic characterizations of LCP codes, showing that for constacyclic and quasi-cyclic LCPs, the security parameter min(d(C), d(D⊥)) reduces to a single distance. Also gives binary LCP examples with better parameters than known LCD codes and a linear programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
- Adopt from Researcher A: The idea of using LCP structure for fault detection in secure computation is promising, but their reliance on AG codes is not grounded in Paper-c. I reject the elliptic-curve AG construction as unsupported by available sources.
- Qualify: Paper-c’s constacyclic equivalence between C and D⊥ means the two code spaces are algebraically linked, not independent. This makes the LCP pair unsuitable as two independent secret shares, because knowledge of one share may reveal information about the other.
- Revised mechanism: Use the single-distance property of quasi-cyclic LCP codes as a lightweight integrity check for a single encoded message, not as a two-share scheme. The syndrome of D⊥ acts as a zero-redundancy authentication tag for data encoded in C.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Construct a binary quasi-cyclic LCP pair (C,D) with n=2m, index 2, using double circulant examples from Paper-c.
- Encode message m ∈ C. Compute syndrome s = H_{D⊥} · y for received word y.
- Test: For a tampering adversary flipping ≤ t bits, measure probability that s remains in the correct coset. Compare against an LCD code of same length and dimension.
- Validation: Use the linear programming bound from Paper-c to show the LCP scheme matches the best LCD minimum distance while adding an independent failure mode for the adversary. Reject Researcher A’s MPC simulation as not grounded in Paper-c.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose a single-code dual-purpose reliability–security scheme using binary quasi-cyclic LCP codes. The constacyclic equivalence between C and D⊥ reduces security analysis to one distance parameter, while the double circulant structure enables efficient encoding. Unlike two-share secret sharing, this scheme adds a zero-redundancy integrity check to error correction, with preliminary examples suggesting performance matching or exceeding LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Exploit the single-distance property of quasi-cyclic LCP codes to add a zero-redundancy authentication tag to error-correcting codes, improving on LCD code security without extra storage.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper A contributes a concrete method for quantifying cell-level mechanical stress via fluorescent tension sensors, with calibration data and a defined analysis pipeline.
- Paper B contributes a theory of how tissue curvature feeds back onto epithelial proliferation through morphogen gradient distortion, with a computational model and predicted growth fields.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Mechanical stress (A) and curvature-modulated morphogen signaling (B) are causally linked if stress alters the effective diffusivity or receptor binding of the morphogen. This is operationally testable: curvature-induced stress gradients should predict local changes in morphogen gradient slope, measurable with the sensor system from A and the gradient readout from B.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Use an in vitro epithelial dome or gut-organoid system where curvature is controlled by substrate geometry. Measure tension-sensor fluorescence (A) across dome apex vs. base. Simultaneously image a fluorescently tagged morphogen (e.g., a BMP or Wnt reporter) and extract local gradient steepness. Validate sensor calibration using known osmotic or laser-ablation stress. Then compare two conditions: (1) wild-type tissue, (2) tissue with stress-insensitive morphogen receptor or altered extracellular matrix stiffness. Prediction: in wild-type, high-stress regions show flattened morphogen gradients and reduced proliferation; in stress-insensitive condition, gradient flattening is absent. Statistical validation via spatial regression of stress on gradient slope, controlling for curvature.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
Epithelial tissues integrate mechanical and biochemical cues during growth, but whether curvature-driven stress directly reshapes morphogen gradients is unknown. We combine a calibrated fluorescent tension-sensor method with a curvature-morphogen feedback model to test whether stress gradients flatten signaling gradients and alter proliferation. Using geometrically controlled epithelial domes, we will map stress and morphogen slope simultaneously, then perturb stress sensing to isolate the mechanical contribution. This would provide the first causal link between tissue-scale curvature, cell-level stress, and morphogen gradient shape, beyond either source paper.

FINAL IDEA: Curvature-induced mechanical stress gradients actively flatten morphogen signaling gradients, providing a mechanochemical mechanism for curvature-dependent growth control.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper A (tension sensors): calibrated fluorescent method for cell-level mechanical stress mapping.
- Paper B (curvature–morphogen model): computational theory linking tissue curvature to morphogen gradient distortion and proliferation.
- Paper C (LCP codes): algebraic construction showing constacyclic/quasi-cyclic LCP pairs reduce security to a single distance parameter, with binary examples and a linear programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
I reject Researcher B’s coding-only integration as insufficiently cross-disciplinary. Instead, I adopt Paper C’s algebraic equivalence between C and D⊥ as a formal analog for a biological dual-function structure: mechanical stress (A) and morphogen signaling (B) may form an “error-correcting” pair where stress gradients encode curvature information redundantly with morphogen gradients. The operational bridge is that constacyclic equivalence in codes corresponds to a geometric invariance in tissues—curvature-induced stress and morphogen gradient shape are two representations of the same underlying curvature field, each providing an independent “check” on the other.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Use epithelial dome cultures with controlled curvature. Measure tension-sensor fluorescence (A) and morphogen gradient steepness (B) simultaneously. Define a “tissue code” where stress values at discrete positions form codeword C, and morphogen gradient slopes form codeword D. Test whether C and D⊥ (the dual of D under a discrete Fourier transform over the dome’s angular positions) satisfy the constacyclic equivalence from Paper C. Validation: compute the minimum distance of the tissue code (min(d(C), d(D⊥))) and test whether this single parameter predicts proliferation error rates better than either stress or morphogen alone. Perturb stress sensing (e.g., YAP knockout) and check whether the algebraic equivalence breaks, as predicted if stress and morphogen are redundant encodings of curvature.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose that epithelial tissues use curvature-induced stress and morphogen gradients as dual, algebraically equivalent encodings of geometric information, analogous to linear complementary pairs of codes. By mapping tension-sensor and morphogen readouts onto a quasi-cyclic code structure, we test whether a single distance parameter—min(d(stress), d(morphogen⊥))—predicts growth fidelity better than either signal alone. This would establish a formal, testable link between mechanical and biochemical signaling as redundant error-correcting channels.

FINAL IDEA: Curvature-induced stress and morphogen gradients form a biological linear complementary pair whose single algebraic distance parameter predicts growth fidelity, uniting mechanical and biochemical signaling as redundant error-correcting codes.
